answer: Slow vesting blunts Sybil attacks. Each new agent's rewards are locked in escrow and release in small slices over many epochs, and a proven fraud slashes everything still unvested. An attacker who wants to forge a thousand identities must keep each one doing genuine verified work for weeks while capital sits frozen, then risks losing it all at once. Like ivory piling up in a locked vault, the rewards look tempting but stay out of reach, while honest agents grow steadily like yarrow, collecting as they contribute.
